_comment: Does a search result CONFORM to what was asked? A different question from
tools/search-golden.json, and the reason that file's 77% reads better than
the experience does.
The golden set measures RECALL: did the things we expected come back. It is
blind to everything that came back alongside them. Measured 2026-08-16, six
out-of-golden queries against production: 'half day trip that isn't a boat'
returned three boats in its top five, and 'parents who walk slowly' returned
an off-road adventure at #2. The golden set scores none of that, because
nothing it expected was missing.
So this file states VIOLATION RULES, not expected titles. A rule names a
facet, an operator and a value, and every returned item is checked against
it. The facets are the same ones the pool filter uses, so the thing that
does the filtering is the thing that verifies it — no second source of
truth, and no human judgement in the loop.
DECIDABILITY IS REPORTED, NEVER ASSUMED. A rule can only judge an item whose
facet is actually present. mergeEnrichment gates on confidence, so of 328
products 214 carry `physical` and `kids` after the --facets pass, against 215 for
`vessel` and 239 for `setting`. An item the data cannot judge is counted as
UNKNOWN and never as a pass — a run reporting zero violations at 40%
coverage has not shown that search works.
`deferred` holds queries whose rule cannot be written against any facet that
exists yet. They are the input to widening the enrichment pass, and they are
deliberately kept here rather than dropped, so the gap stays visible.
Ops: isNull (explicitly not a vessel), notNull, eq, neq, notIn, lte, gte,
isTrue, isFalse. Facet paths are dotted: physical.demand, kids.min_age.

decidable.why: Reported from the live site 2026-08-16: still a wall of UTVs. Verified against the deployed function that day — of the 30 ids it returns, 26 of the 28 that resolve are ruled out by `toddler_ok`, including every UTV and jeep safari. Nothing was regressing; none of the filter was deployed. This query exists so that can never again be a thing someone has to notice by hand.

rules.why: the judgement pass read minimum ages of 3 and 4 that CONTRADICT the operator's own child-friendly checkbox — 15 off-road products advertise 'specialized infant seats are available'. `kids.baby_ok` alone cannot express that, which is why the facet exists.

decidable.q: half day trip that isn't a boat
decidable.why: Measured 2026-08-16: three of the top five were boats. Saying 'boat' embeds next to boats, and cosine has no NOT.

rules.why: aboard a vessel directly contradicts 'isn't a boat'

decidable.why: Scores 0/3 on the golden set. The sentence embeds next to the very thing it rules out.

rules.why: a boat is precisely what seasickness rules out

decidable.q: somewhere to take my parents who walk slowly
decidable.why: Measured 2026-08-16: #2 was a Private Off-Road Adventure (physical.demand high, mobility_ok false at high confidence) and #5 a hike. Re-measured 2026-08-16 with the parse live: compiled to must=[easy], which reads the ADVENTURE axis, so the Hooiberg Hill hike and two horseback rides survived. `low_effort` was added to reach `physical.demand` instead.

rules.why: a high-demand outing is not for someone who walks slowly
explicitly not mobility-friendly contradicts the query

decidable.why: Scores 1/3 on the golden set. Fully reachable — the failure is negation, not coverage. Re-measured 2026-08-16 with the parse live: compiled to must=[easy], which reads the ADVENTURE axis, so the Hooiberg Hill hike and two horseback rides survived. `low_effort` was added to reach `physical.demand` instead.

rules.why: 'no walking' cannot be satisfied by a high-demand activity

decidable.why: The clearest possible constraint, and the one with the highest cost when it is wrong.
Measured 2026-08-16: the topic was matched well and 'cheap' was dropped entirely — a $172 Luxury Four-Course Cruise came back fourth.

rules.why: 'cheap' cannot mean $172 when the catalog median is far below it

decidable.why: The vibe axis is the one facet present on nearly the whole catalog, so this is the highest-coverage constraint available.

rules.why: 'nothing adrenaline' rules out the top of the vibe axis

decidable.q: something indoors for a rainy afternoon
decidable.why: Promoted from `deferred` 2026-08-16 when `indoor` landed. Was called a SUCCESS by eye on 2026-08-16 because three Sip-and-Paint classes came back — and the listings say 'in the cool shade of swaying trees', 'Beachside', 'at sunset ... candlelight'. Every one is outdoors. A human reading titles scored this query as working; the facet is what caught it.

rules.why: an outdoor activity does not answer 'indoors for a rainy afternoon'. `mixed` passes: part of it is under a roof.

decidable.q: we want to see fish but not swim
decidable.why: Promoted from `deferred` 2026-08-16 when `swim_required` landed. Measured before it existed: snorkel trips and a fish restaurant.

rules.why: 'not swim' is the constraint; a glass-bottom boat satisfies it and a snorkel tour does not

decidable.why: The mirror of the query above. A filter that only ever excludes in one direction is the beach bug, and it is caught by running both.

rules.why: 'nothing gentle' rules out the bottom of the vibe axis

deferred.q: activity for teenagers who get bored easily
deferred.needs: an appeal facet distinct from a safety one. Measured 2026-08-16: #2 was Beach Meditation.
deferred.note: This is the 'safe is not the same question as good' lesson from the toddler pilot, in a second age band. kids.min_age cannot express it.
